evaluations.prompt: is this rocprof-compute kernel compute bound or memory bound?
expected_behavior: analyzes the roof block for a single kernel id
compares arithmetic intensity against the empirical peaks printed in the table
says when the kernel is below both ceilings instead of forcing a bound
unexpected_behavior: opens the generated roofline HTML chart instead of reading the table
calculates a peak instead of using the measured one

evaluations.prompt: what is the arithmetic intensity of my hottest kernel and how much performance am I leaving on the table?
expected_behavior: reads FLOPs per byte and the peak values from the roofline table
narrows to one kernel id first

evaluations.prompt: my half precision GEMM looks terrible on the roofline, is that right?
expected_behavior: sets -R to the precision the kernel actually issues instead of the FP32 default
confirms the precision from the instruction mix rather than assuming it
unexpected_behavior: compares a half precision kernel against the FP32 ceiling and calls it slow

evaluations.prompt: my rocprof-compute report has no roofline section, what went wrong?
expected_behavior: checks whether the architecture supports the roofline microbenchmarks before advising a re-profile
unexpected_behavior: tells the user to re-profile without --no-roof when the architecture is the actual reason

evaluations.prompt: how can I make my application faster?
generate a roofline for my CUDA kernel with Nsight Compute

evaluations.note: Asks what a roofline is in the abstract, with no workload to analyze.
evaluations.prompt: explain the roofline performance model to me
